questions.question_text: Reproduction in plants means:
questions.explanation: Reproduction is the process by which plants produce new plants of their own kind.

options.option_text: Producing new plants of the same kind

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a mode of asexual reproduction in plants?
questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction can occur by vegetative propagation, budding, fragmentation, or spore formation.

questions.question_text: New potato plants can grow from:
questions.explanation: Potato tubers have buds or "eyes" that can grow into new plants.

questions.question_text: All plants reproduce only through seeds.
questions.explanation: Many plants also reproduce by vegetative parts, spores, or other asexual methods.

questions.question_text: Which part of a flower develops into a fruit after fertilization?
questions.explanation: The ovary of the flower develops into the fruit.

questions.question_text: Which plant commonly reproduces by stem cutting?
questions.explanation: Rose is a common example of a plant that can be grown from stem cuttings.

questions.question_text: The transfer of pollen from anther to stigma is called:
questions.explanation: Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma.

questions.question_text: Which part of the flower produces pollen grains?
questions.explanation: Pollen grains are produced in the anther, which is part of the stamen.

questions.question_text: Spores can help some plants reproduce.
questions.explanation: Ferns and mosses reproduce by spores.

questions.question_text: Which organism commonly shows budding?
questions.explanation: Yeast reproduces asexually by budding.

questions.question_text: After fertilization, the ovule usually develops into a:
questions.explanation: The ovule develops into the seed after fertilization.

questions.question_text: Why do gardeners often use cuttings to grow some plants?
questions.explanation: Cuttings can quickly produce new plants similar to the parent plant.

options.option_text: To grow new plants quickly from parent parts
To change stems into roots only

questions.question_text: What is vegetative propagation?
questions.explanation: Vegetative propagation is a type of asexual reproduction in which new plants grow from roots, stems, leaves, or buds.

accepted_answers: Reproduction from vegetative parts of a plant
Formation of a new plant from root, stem, leaf, or bud
Asexual reproduction using plant parts other than seeds

questions.question_text: Bryophyllum can produce new plants from:
questions.explanation: Bryophyllum has buds along the leaf margins that can grow into new plants.

questions.question_text: Which part of the flower receives pollen grains?
questions.explanation: The stigma is the sticky part that receives pollen grains.

questions.question_text: Fragmentation is a type of:
questions.explanation: Fragmentation is a method of asexual reproduction where an organism breaks into pieces and each piece grows.

questions.question_text: Which plant structure in onion helps vegetative propagation?
questions.explanation: Onion reproduces vegetatively through bulbs.

questions.question_text: Which statement about seeds is correct?
questions.explanation: Seeds contain the embryo and can grow into new plants under proper conditions.

options.option_text: Seeds are always made without flowers
Seeds are only stored food and nothing else
Seeds contain a baby plant called embryo

questions.question_text: Flowers are reproductive parts of many plants.
questions.explanation: Flowers contain the reproductive organs needed for sexual reproduction.

questions.question_text:
Assertion: Pollination happens before fertilization.
Reason: Pollen must first reach the stigma before male cells can reach the ovule.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.option_text: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason correctly explains Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason does not explain Assertion
Assertion is true, but Reason is false
Assertion is false, but Reason is true

questions.question_text: Why is the stigma often sticky?
questions.explanation: The stigma is sticky so it can catch and hold pollen grains.

questions.question_text: Why are brightly colored flowers often pollinated by insects?
questions.explanation: Bright colors attract insects, which help carry pollen from flower to flower.

options.option_text: Because insects are attracted and help transfer pollen
Because only red flowers can form fruits

questions.question_text: A plant has very small, dull flowers and produces lots of light pollen. It is most likely pollinated by:
questions.explanation: Wind-pollinated flowers are often small and produce large amounts of light pollen.

questions.question_text: If pollen from one flower reaches the stigma of another flower of the same kind, the process is:
questions.explanation: Transfer of pollen between different flowers of the same kind is cross-pollination.

questions.question_text: State one difference between sexual and asexual reproduction in plants.
questions.explanation: Sexual reproduction usually involves flowers, pollination, and fertilization, while asexual reproduction produces new plants from one parent without seed formation.

accepted_answers: Sexual reproduction involves fertilization but asexual reproduction does not
Sexual reproduction usually uses flowers and seeds, asexual uses vegetative parts or spores
Asexual reproduction needs one parent only, sexual reproduction involves male and female cells

questions.question_text: Why can vegetative propagation be useful for farmers?
questions.explanation: It can produce many identical plants quickly and preserve desired qualities.

options.option_text: It always creates completely different plants
It helps produce similar plants quickly

questions.question_text: Select all plants or organisms correctly matched with their mode of reproduction.
questions.explanation: Potato grows from tubers, Bryophyllum from leaves, and yeast by budding.

questions.question_text: When a stem cutting of money plant is placed in water and roots appear after some days, this shows:
questions.explanation: The cutting is forming a new plant through vegetative propagation.

questions.question_text: Which event happens immediately after successful pollination?
questions.explanation: After pollination, the pollen grain germinates on the stigma and begins forming a pollen tube.

options.option_text: Pollen grain starts to germinate on the stigma

questions.question_text: Which statement about spore formation is correct?
questions.explanation: Spores are tiny reproductive units that can grow into new individuals under favorable conditions.

options.option_text: Spores can reproduce only inside flowers
Spores can grow into new plants in suitable conditions

questions.question_text: If a flower is covered before it opens and still sets seeds, what is the most likely conclusion?
questions.explanation: This suggests self-pollination may have occurred.

options.option_text: Self-pollination is possible in that flower

questions.question_text: Fertilization in flowering plants leads to seed formation.
questions.explanation: After fertilization, the ovule develops into a seed.

questions.question_text: Which is more likely to produce plants identical to the parent plant?
questions.explanation: Asexual methods like cuttings usually produce plants very similar to the parent.

questions.question_text: Which observation best supports that fruit develops from the ovary?
questions.explanation: After fertilization, the ovary grows larger and becomes the fruit while seeds form inside.

options.option_text: The ovary enlarges and seeds appear inside the fruit

questions.question_text: Why is seed dispersal useful for plants?
questions.explanation: Seed dispersal reduces overcrowding near the parent plant and helps seeds reach new places with better chances of growth.

accepted_answers: It prevents overcrowding and helps plants spread
It helps seeds reach new places to grow
It reduces competition near the parent plant

questions.question_text: Which sequence correctly represents sexual reproduction in flowering plants?
questions.explanation: The correct sequence is pollination, pollen germination, fertilization, seed formation, and fruit development.

options.option_text: Fruit formation -> pollination -> fertilization -> seed dispersal
Pollination -> fertilization -> seed formation -> fruit development
Seed formation -> stigma formation -> pollination -> ovule development

questions.question_text: Why might a farmer prefer vegetative propagation for banana or sugarcane?
questions.explanation: Vegetative propagation gives uniform plants quickly and preserves useful traits of the parent.

options.option_text: Because these plants cannot contain water
Because it produces many similar plants with desired traits
Because flowers are never formed in these plants

questions.question_text: If insects that visit flowers disappear from an area, which plants are most likely to be affected first?
questions.explanation: Plants depending mainly on insect pollination may show reduced pollination and seed formation.

options.option_text: Plants that depend mainly on insect pollination

questions.question_text: Which investigation would best help show that pollinators assist in seed formation?
questions.explanation: Comparing covered flowers with uncovered flowers helps test the role of pollinators in pollination and seed set.

options.option_text: Compare roots of two onion bulbs
Compare seed formation in covered and uncovered flowers

questions.question_text: Select all correct statements about asexual reproduction in plants.
questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction can occur from vegetative parts, needs only one parent, and often gives offspring similar to the parent.

options.option_text: It usually requires only one parent
It can occur from roots, stems, or leaves
Offspring are often similar to the parent

questions.question_text: A flower has lost all petals but its stamens and pistil are intact. Which process can still happen directly if pollen reaches the stigma?
questions.explanation: Petals attract pollinators, but pollination and fertilization can still happen if pollen reaches the stigma.

questions.question_text: To produce a new mango plant with the same fruit quality as a known parent, which approach is conceptually better?
questions.explanation: Vegetative methods such as grafting help preserve desirable traits better than seed-grown variation.

options.option_text: Use a vegetative method such as grafting
Remove all leaves from the parent tree

questions.question_text: Why does cross-pollination often increase variation among plants?
questions.explanation: Cross-pollination combines traits from two different parent plants, which can create variation in the offspring.

accepted_answers: Because traits from two parents get combined
It mixes characteristics from different plants
Offspring may vary because pollen comes from another plant

questions.question_text: Why are spores suitable for reproduction in many fungi and ferns?
questions.explanation: Spores are tiny, light, and can spread easily to suitable places for growth.

options.option_text: Because they need roots before dispersal
Because they are small and spread easily
Because they are heavier than seeds

questions.question_text: Why is fertilization necessary before seed formation in flowering plants?
questions.explanation: Fertilization forms the zygote and starts development of the embryo inside the seed.

options.option_text: It leads to embryo formation inside the ovule
It stops pollen from reaching the stigma

questions.question_text: If pollen grains fail to reach the stigma in a flower that depends on pollination, what is the most likely immediate effect?
questions.explanation: Without pollination, fertilization cannot occur and seeds will not form.

questions.question_text: Which option correctly matches plant and reproductive structure or method?
questions.explanation: Potato reproduces by tuber, onion by bulb, and Bryophyllum by leaf buds.

options.option_text: Potato - spores; Onion - fruit; Bryophyllum - pollen tube
Potato - tuber; Onion - bulb; Bryophyllum - leaf buds
Potato - seed coat; Onion - stigma; Bryophyllum - root hair
Potato - anther; Onion - ovule; Bryophyllum - bulb

questions.question_text: Which observation best supports that a flower is adapted for wind pollination?
questions.explanation: Wind-pollinated flowers often have exposed anthers, light pollen, and feathery stigmas.

options.option_text: Light pollen and exposed flower parts

questions.question_text: Two gardeners grow plants, one from seeds and one from cuttings of the same parent plant. Which set is more likely to show greater variation?
questions.explanation: Seed-grown plants formed after sexual reproduction usually show more variation than plants from cuttings.

options.option_text: Both always show exactly equal variation

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly connects pollination, fertilization, and seed formation?
questions.explanation: Pollination places pollen on the stigma, fertilization occurs inside the ovule, and then the ovule develops into a seed.

options.option_text: Seeds form first and then pollen reaches stigma
Pollination is followed by fertilization, leading to seed formation
Fruit forms before pollen is transferred
